title: Do I have to file?
subject: Money

text: A short course on whether the average worker needs a 2025 federal return.
Figures are for tax year 2025, filed in 2026. They change. Check IRS.gov.
Most people file if their gross income is at least the standard deduction for their status.
Single, under 65: $15,750. Married filing jointly, both under 65: $31,500. Head of household, under 65: $23,625.
Exceptions that still require a return
Self-employment net earnings of $400 or more: file, even if wages are low.
Married filing separately: file if gross income is $5 or more. Advance premium tax credit: file. You want a refund of withholding: file.
Filing status is set on December 31
Single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse.
Head of household is not a vibe. You must be unmarried, pay more than half the cost of the home, and have a qualifying person.
You are single, under 65, and your only income is $14,000 in wages. Must you file?

choices.label: No. $14,000 is under the $15,750 single threshold.
Yes. Everyone with a job must file.
Yes. The threshold for single is $5.

text: File if you are over the threshold, have $400 of self-employment earnings, are married filing separately, or want a refund.
Status is decided on December 31. Confirm the year's numbers on IRS.gov.

notes: Example course. Tax year 2025 figures, filed in 2026. Confirm on IRS.gov. Not tax advice.
